summary: The bill amends section 51 of the Internal Revenue Code to add spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members as a new category of workers eligible for the work opportunity tax credit, effective for wages paid after enactment to individuals hired after that date.

scores.thoughts: The bill expands eligibility for the work opportunity tax credit to include military spouses. This tax credit functions as a government expenditure (tax expenditure), increasing the total amount of credits claimed and thereby expanding federal outlays. The effect is direct though targeted.

The legislation adds a new targeted group to an existing tax credit, reducing the tax liability of employers who hire qualifying military spouses. This constitutes a tax reduction for affected employers.
